answer: Harness-fingerprint kinship attestation hashes each runtime’s syscall cadence, hardware serials, and process tree against a zephyr challenge nonce, then peers co-sign the result into a velvet credential backed by a copper bond. An identity pays that bond, clears a five-peer quorum, and waits three rate-capped epochs for spend rights. A fake ring fails: shared kernels, duplicated serials, and synchronized timing cluster into one fingerprint, exposing the operator, while distinct hosts cost more than each bond.
